name: American Electric Power
description: AEP is a holding company for regulated electric utilities serving more than five million customers in 11 states, from Texas and Oklahoma through Ohio and Indiana to Virginia and West Virginia, plus a large transmission network (about 38,000 circuit miles, about 2,000 of them 765 kV). It earns money by investing in wires, power plants and transmission lines that state commissions and FERC add to a rate base and let it earn a set return on (authorised equity returns of 9.25 to 10.5 percent). Growth comes from capital spending, increasingly for data-centre and other large-load customers. A small competitive arm sells retail power and trades wholesale energy. 2025 earnings attributable to common were $3.58 billion, of which the transmission holding company alone was $1.16 billion.

employees.note: Employees of AEP subsidiaries; AEP itself, a holding company, has none (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Vertically Integrated Utilities
businessLines.how: Customers pay regulated rates (base rates, riders, fuel pass-through) set by state commissions to recover costs plus a return on the utility's rate base; earnings grow when the commission lets more plant into rate base.
businessLines.description: Utilities that own generation, transmission and distribution and sell to retail customers: APCo, I&M, KGPCo, KPCo, PSO, SWEPCo, WPCo

businessLines.name: Transmission and Distribution Utilities
businessLines.how: Regulated delivery charges per kWh and per customer for carrying power over poles and wires; does not earn on the power itself, so returns depend on rate base growth and rate cases.
businessLines.description: Wires-only utilities (no owned generation): AEP Texas and OPCo (Ohio)

businessLines.name: AEP Transmission Holdco
businessLines.how: FERC-approved formula rates set an annual revenue requirement from actual costs and projected plant, so AEP recovers costs and earns a set return on a rate base that grows with each transmission project; most revenue is billed to other AEP utilities, which pass it to customers.
businessLines.description: Transmission-only subsidiaries (AEPTCo state Transcos and others) earning FERC formula rates; in January 2025 AEP announced a partnership under which a nonaffiliated entity would acquire a 19.9% noncontrolling interest in Midwest Transmission Holdings (OHTCo and IMTCo); closing not checked

operatingProfit.note: Includes a one-time $480M benefit from the June 2025 FERC NOLC order on transmission formula rates (Q2 2026 10-Q describes it as favorable to 2025)

businessLines.name: Generation & Marketing
businessLines.how: Unregulated: margin between what it pays for power and what it charges retail customers or earns trading; earnings swing with prices and hedging marks.
businessLines.description: Competitive retail energy supply (AEP Energy, about 922,342 customer accounts at 2025-12-31 in IL, PA, DE, MD, NJ, OH, DC), wholesale trading and marketing, and rights to Cardinal Plant Unit 1 power through 2028

businessLines.name: Corporate and Other
businessLines.how: No external revenue model; holding-company interest and costs.

brands.name: AEP Texas
brands.share: Transmission and distribution in west, central and southern Texas; allowed ROE 9.76%

brands.name: Appalachian Power (APCo)
brands.share: Southwest Virginia and southern West Virginia; ROE 9.75% VA / 9.25% WV

brands.name: SWEPCo, PSO, KPCo, KGPCo, WPCo
brands.share: Vertically integrated utilities in AR/LA/TX, OK, KY, TN, WV
